plan.description: Strongest cloud model on every placement unit: gpt-5.5-cloud

Hybrid cost/latency exploration: keep the strongest model only for user-facing final answer generation, move branch/control decisions to the cheaper structured/tool-capable cloud model, and offload non-user-facing question rewriting to the free local model.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: Requires structured output and controls branching, so use gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for reliability while substantially reducing the high per-call cost of the baseline gpt-5.5-cloud router.
rationale.generate_answer: Final answer quality is the most user-visible metric; retain gpt-5.5-cloud here to preserve answer synthesis quality from retrieved context.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: This unit requires tool calling and branch control and is invoked most often; gpt-4.1-mini-cloud supports tool calling and should cut cost/latency versus gpt-5.5-cloud while maintaining adequate routing/query behavior.
rationale.rewrite_question: Question rewrite is non-user-facing, does not require tools or structured output, and has fewer invocations; qwen-local is capability-compatible and zero cloud cost, making it useful to test local offload impact without risking final answer formatting.

plan.description: Low-cost cloud-only exploration: use gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for every placement unit to quantify the quality impact of replacing the expensive final-answer model while preserving reliable tool calling, structured routing, and low latency across all control nodes.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: This unit requires structured output and branch control. Candidate-1 already showed gpt-4.1-mini-cloud handled this role with much lower cost and latency than gpt-5.5-cloud, so keep it on the cheaper structured-capable cloud endpoint.
rationale.generate_answer: Candidate-1 retained gpt-5.5-cloud here, but this unit dominated remaining cloud cost and latency. Moving final answer generation to gpt-4.1-mini-cloud tests whether much lower cost and faster responses can preserve acceptable answer quality given retrieved context.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: This entry unit requires tool calling and branch control and is invoked most frequently. Candidate-1 showed gpt-4.1-mini-cloud is capability-compatible and dramatically cheaper/faster than gpt-5.5-cloud, so keep it here.
rationale.rewrite_question: Use gpt-4.1-mini-cloud rather than qwen-local to keep the plan cloud-only and avoid the observed local rewrite latency in candidate-1, while maintaining strong query rewrite reliability at negligible expected cost due to low invocation frequency.

plan.description: Hybrid capability/cost exploration: retain the strongest model for final user-facing answer quality, keep the structured retrieval sufficiency router on the proven low-cost cloud model, move the high-frequency initial tool-calling controller to the free local tool-capable endpoint to test cloud-cost reduction, and use fast cheap cloud for rare question rewrites instead of the slower local rewrite observed previously.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: This router requires structured output and branch control. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud already showed reliable capability compatibility at far lower cost and latency than gpt-5.5-cloud in candidates 1 and 2, so it remains the best exploratory choice for this non-user-facing control step.
rationale.generate_answer: Candidate-1 achieved the strongest aggregate quality among evaluated non-baseline plans with gpt-5.5-cloud as final answer generator, while candidate-2 lost quality when this unit moved to gpt-4.1-mini-cloud. Keeping gpt-5.5-cloud here isolates whether further cost savings can come from controller offload without sacrificing answer synthesis quality.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: This is the most frequently invoked unit and requires tool calling and branch control. qwen-local supports tool calling and structured output with a sufficient 32768-token context window, and using it here tests a substantially lower cloud-cost point not yet evaluated, accepting potential latency/quality risk for exploration.
rationale.rewrite_question: Rewrite is rare but candidate-1 showed local rewrite latency was high for its single invocation. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud is cheap, fast, and capable for this non-structured rewrite role, so assigning it here avoids repeating the prior local-rewrite hybrid while limiting added cloud cost.

plan.description: Targeted local-offload exploration: keep the high-performing candidate-1 pattern for final answer generation and the frequent tool-calling entry controller, but move only the structured retrieval sufficiency router to the free local endpoint while keeping rare rewrites on the fast cheap cloud endpoint. This tests whether the non-user-facing structured branch router can be localized to reduce cloud cost, without repeating prior maps or moving the final answer off gpt-5.5-cloud.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: This unit requires structured output and branch control; qwen-local supports structured output and has sufficient context. Prior runs show this router is invoked often and accounts for measurable cloud cost on gpt-4.1-mini (~$0.04) or much more on gpt-5.5, so localizing it is a capability-compatible way to explore additional cost savings. Candidate-3 showed localizing the entry controller hurt latency/quality, but this router is non-user-facing and simpler than tool-calling query generation.
rationale.generate_answer: Keep gpt-5.5-cloud for the final user-facing answer because candidate-1 had the best aggregate quality among previous candidates (exact match 0.64, F1 0.775) when the final generator used gpt-5.5, while all-mini reduced quality. This isolates the effect of localizing the router rather than confounding with answer synthesis degradation.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: Use gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for the initial tool-calling controller because it performed well in candidates 1 and 2 with much lower latency and cost than baseline, whereas candidate-3's qwen-local controller increased mean latency and lowered exact match. This preserves reliable tool use and branch control at low cost.
rationale.rewrite_question: Use gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for rare rewrites: candidate-1's qwen-local rewrite had high latency for its single invocation, while candidate-2/3 showed gpt-4.1-mini rewrites are extremely cheap and fast. This also avoids repeating any evaluated assignment map.

plan.description: Latency/cost stress test with a cheap cloud final answerer and strongest cloud control: keep all branch-critical retrieval/query decisions on gpt-5.5-cloud to test whether stronger routing can recover evidence quality, while moving final answer generation to gpt-4.1-mini-cloud to avoid the high cost/latency seen when gpt-5.5 handles answer synthesis. Use gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for rare rewrites because prior runs showed it is fast and negligible-cost compared with local rewrite.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: This structured branch router has only been tested on all-gpt-5.5 baseline or cheaper/local hybrids. Reintroducing gpt-5.5 here, while not using it for final answer, isolates whether the strongest retrieval sufficiency decisions improve routing/retrieval quality relative to the all-mini and local-router candidates. It supports structured output and the context window is sufficient.
rationale.generate_answer: Prior candidates show gpt-5.5 final generation yields higher quality but dominates cloud cost and latency; candidate-2 showed gpt-4.1-mini final generation is much faster and cheaper with moderate quality. Assigning gpt-4.1-mini here explores a new trade-off: spend model budget on upstream control rather than answer synthesis.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: This user-facing entry controller requires tool calling and branch control. Using gpt-5.5-cloud tests whether stronger initial query/tool decisions improve retrieval outcomes over gpt-4.1-mini or qwen-local controllers, while remaining capability-compatible.
rationale.rewrite_question: Question rewrite is rare and does not require tools or structured output. Previous evaluations showed gpt-4.1-mini rewrites were extremely cheap and fast, while qwen-local rewrite could be slow, so this keeps rewrite latency low without material cost.

plan.description: Refined high-quality hybrid: keep the best-performing candidate-1 core with gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for frequent structured/tool control and gpt-5.5-cloud for final user-facing answer synthesis, but move rare question rewrites from qwen-local to gpt-4.1-mini-cloud to test whether the local rewrite latency observed in candidate-1 can be avoided with negligible added cloud cost. This complete assignment has not been evaluated previously.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: Requires structured output and branch control. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud is capability-compatible and consistently much cheaper/faster than gpt-5.5 for this router; candidate-1 achieved the strongest aggregate answer quality with this router on mini, while candidate-4's local router increased latency and cost indirectly.
rationale.generate_answer: Final answer generation is user-facing and previous results indicate quality is strongest when this unit remains on gpt-5.5-cloud: candidate-1 and candidate-4 both reached 0.64 exact match with gpt-5.5 final generation, whereas all-mini dropped to 0.58 and strong-control/mini-answer dropped to 0.38.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: This high-frequency entry controller requires tool calling and branch control. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud supports tool use and performed better as the controller than qwen-local: candidate-3's local controller increased mean latency and reduced exact match, while candidate-1's mini controller delivered the best F1 and low cost.
rationale.rewrite_question: Question rewriting is rare and does not require tools or structured output. Candidate-1 used qwen-local here and saw a single rewrite take nearly 10 seconds, while candidate-2 and candidate-3 showed gpt-4.1-mini rewrites are fast and extremely low cost. Moving rewrite to mini avoids local latency risk without materially changing cloud spend.

plan.description: Zero-cost final-answer exploration while preserving the strongest observed cheap cloud control pattern: keep all branch-critical routing, tool-calling, and rare rewrite steps on gpt-4.1-mini-cloud, but move only final answer generation to the local qwen endpoint. This previously unevaluated placement tests whether local answer synthesis can reduce cloud cost below all-mini while maintaining the proven mini-based retrieval/control behavior that underpinned candidate-6's strong evidence metrics.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: Requires structured output and branch control. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud has been the most reliable low-cost choice for this router: candidate-6 with mini routing achieved the best aggregate quality (0.70 exact match, 0.835 F1) and better latency than local-router candidate-4, while preserving capability compatibility.
rationale.generate_answer: This is user-facing, so local generation is a quality risk, but qwen-local is capability-compatible for non-tool, non-structured answer generation and has sufficient 32k context. Prior runs have not isolated qwen as the final answerer; this explores a new cost/latency frontier by eliminating the dominant gpt-5.5 final-generation cost from candidate-6 and potentially reducing cloud spend below the all-mini plan.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: Requires tool calling and branch control. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud consistently outperformed local tool control in trade-off terms: candidate-3's qwen controller increased latency and reduced quality, while candidate-6's mini controller contributed to the best overall metrics. Keeping it on mini avoids destabilizing retrieval decisions while changing only the answerer.
rationale.rewrite_question: Rare, non-user-facing, and no structured/tool requirement. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud rewrites were extremely fast and negligible-cost in candidates 2, 3, and 6, whereas qwen-local rewrite showed high latency in candidate-1. Keeping rewrite on mini maintains the best observed latency behavior and avoids repeating any prior assignment map.

plan.description: Local-control / premium-answer exploration: retain gpt-5.5-cloud only for final user-facing answer synthesis, but move all non-final control/rewrite units to qwen-local. This previously unevaluated placement probes the lowest-cloud-cost variant that still uses the strongest answer generator, testing whether local structured routing and tool-calling can preserve enough retrieval quality while eliminating the gpt-4.1-mini control costs seen in candidate-6.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: This router requires structured output and controls branching; qwen-local supports structured output and has a sufficient 32k context window. Candidate-4 showed localizing only this router preserved 0.64 exact match, though with higher latency, so evaluating it alongside local entry control tests a more aggressive cloud-cost reduction point not yet covered.
rationale.generate_answer: Keep final answer generation on gpt-5.5-cloud because runs with this unit on gpt-5.5 produced the best answer quality: candidate-6 reached the strongest aggregate metrics (0.70 exact match, 0.835 F1), whereas moving final answers to gpt-4.1-mini or qwen-local substantially reduced quality. This preserves the most user-facing quality lever while exploring local control.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: This entry controller requires tool calling and branch control, and qwen-local is tool-call capable. Candidate-3 showed localizing this high-frequency unit reduced cloud cost but hurt latency/quality when other control stayed on mini; combining it with local router/rewrite and premium final answer is a new point on the trade-off frontier that further reduces cloud spend.
rationale.rewrite_question: Question rewrite is rare and has no tool or structured-output requirement, making qwen-local capability-compatible. Candidate-1 observed local rewrite latency risk for one invocation, but this unit is infrequent; placing it locally completes the all-local-control stress test while avoiding any repeat of prior assignment maps.

plan.description: Low-cost refinement of the all-mini plan: keep the frequent structured router, final answerer, and tool-calling entry controller on gpt-4.1-mini-cloud, but offload only the rare non-user-facing question rewrite to qwen-local. This previously unevaluated placement explores whether cloud spend can be shaved slightly below the all-mini candidate while preserving the faster, more reliable mini behavior on all high-frequency and user-facing units.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: This unit requires structured output and controls branching. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud is capability-compatible and has consistently been the strongest low-cost control choice: candidate-2 achieved very low latency and cost with all-mini routing, while localizing this router in candidate-4 increased latency substantially.
rationale.generate_answer: Moving final answer generation to gpt-4.1-mini-cloud trades off quality for large cost and latency savings. Candidate-2 showed all-mini answer generation was much cheaper and faster than gpt-5.5 final generation, with moderate quality, whereas qwen-local final generation in candidate-7 severely degraded answer quality. Keeping this unit on mini rather than local preserves a more reliable cheap answerer.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: This entry unit is high-frequency, user-facing, requires tool calling, and controls retrieval branching. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud supports tool use and delivered the best latency/cost behavior among capable controllers; qwen-local control in candidates 3 and 8 raised latency and did not improve aggregate quality, while gpt-5.5 control in candidate-5 was costly and lower quality.
rationale.rewrite_question: Question rewriting is rare, non-user-facing, and does not require tools or structured output, so qwen-local is capability-compatible and zero cloud cost. Prior local rewrite latency was high for one candidate-1 invocation, but the unit is infrequent; this isolates the effect of localizing only the least critical unit while avoiding any previously evaluated assignment map.

plan.description: Premium-rewrite variant of the best observed hybrid: keep the candidate-6 core with gpt-4.1-mini-cloud for frequent structured/tool control and gpt-5.5-cloud for final answer synthesis, but assign the rare question rewrite step to gpt-5.5-cloud. This previously unevaluated map tests whether a stronger rewrite model can improve difficult follow-up retrieval cases with only limited additional cost, since rewrites have been infrequent under the mini-control pattern.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: Requires structured output and branch control. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud is capability-compatible and was the most reliable low-cost router in prior runs; the best aggregate run, candidate-6, used mini here and achieved 0.70 exact match, 0.835 answer F1, and strong supporting-title metrics with much lower cost/latency than all-gpt-5.5.
rationale.generate_answer: Final answer generation is user-facing and has been the strongest quality lever. Runs with gpt-5.5-cloud as the answer generator consistently outperformed mini or local answer generation, while candidate-7 showed qwen-local final answers severely degraded quality. Retaining gpt-5.5 here preserves the best observed answer synthesis behavior.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: This high-frequency entry unit requires tool calling and branch control. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud supports the required endpoint capabilities and produced better trade-offs than qwen-local or gpt-5.5 control: local control increased latency in candidates 3 and 8, while gpt-5.5 control in candidate-5 was expensive and low quality.
rationale.rewrite_question: The rewrite unit is rare, non-user-facing, and capability-compatible with gpt-5.5-cloud. Candidate-6 showed the mini-rewrite version of this core was the strongest overall, but hard cases still failed; moving only the rewrite to gpt-5.5 explores whether premium reformulation can improve subsequent retrieval on those difficult examples while adding little expected cost because rewrites have typically occurred only about once under the mini-control pattern.

plan.description: Untested premium-router / mini-tool hybrid: keep the best observed user-facing final answer model on gpt-5.5-cloud and the proven fast cheap rewrite on gpt-4.1-mini-cloud, but swap only the retrieval sufficiency router from the candidate-6 all-mini-control core to gpt-5.5-cloud while leaving the high-frequency initial tool-calling controller on gpt-4.1-mini-cloud. This explores whether stronger structured post-retrieval sufficiency decisions can improve routing/evidence quality without paying the much larger cost of gpt-5.5 for the entry controller or repeating any previous assignment map.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: This unit requires structured output and branch control; gpt-5.5-cloud supports both. Prior runs suggest gpt-4.1-mini routing is usually the best cost/latency choice, but candidate-5’s poor result confounded premium routing with a mini final answer and premium entry controller. Testing only the post-retrieval sufficiency router on gpt-5.5 isolates whether stronger evidence-completeness decisions can improve hard retrieval cases while keeping other high-frequency control cheaper.
rationale.generate_answer: Final answer generation is user-facing and quality-critical. Previous results show placements with gpt-5.5-cloud here dominate quality: candidate-6 achieved the best aggregate exact match and F1, while mini or qwen final generation degraded quality. Keep gpt-5.5 for answer synthesis to preserve the strongest observed user-facing behavior.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: This high-frequency entry unit requires tool calling and branch control. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud is tool-capable and structured-capable, and it produced the best overall trade-off in candidates 1, 2, and especially 6. Avoid gpt-5.5 here because candidate-5’s premium entry control was expensive and low quality, and avoid qwen-local because candidates 3 and 8 showed local entry control increased latency.
rationale.rewrite_question: Question rewriting is rare, non-user-facing, and does not require tools or structured output. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud has been consistently fast and negligible-cost for this step, whereas qwen-local rewrite showed latency risk and gpt-5.5 rewrite in candidate-10 added cost/latency without improving aggregate quality. Keeping mini here isolates the router experiment.

plan.description: Local-router / all-cheap-cloud generation exploration: keep the proven fast, tool-capable gpt-4.1-mini-cloud on the high-frequency initial controller, final answer generation, and rare rewrite step, but move only the structured post-retrieval sufficiency router to qwen-local. This previously unevaluated placement probes whether the router's cloud cost can be eliminated in a low-cost mini-answer configuration while avoiding the severe quality loss from local final answers and the latency/quality issues of local entry control.

rationale.decide_after_retrieval: This unit requires structured output and controls branching; qwen-local supports structured output and has a sufficient 32768-token context. Prior local-router tests with gpt-5.5 final generation (candidate-4) preserved exact match at 0.64 but increased latency, so testing local routing with the cheaper mini final answer isolates whether the router can be offloaded in a budget-oriented setup. This exact combination has not been evaluated.
rationale.generate_answer: Use gpt-4.1-mini-cloud rather than qwen-local because candidate-7 showed local final answers caused a large quality drop (0.26 exact match, 0.452 F1), while all-mini and mini-with-local-rewrite plans retained moderate quality at very low latency/cost. This explores a cheaper final-generation tier than gpt-5.5 without repeating candidate-2 or candidate-9.
rationale.generate_query_or_respond: This high-frequency entry unit is user-facing, requires tool calling, and controls retrieval branching. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud supports tool use and has consistently provided the best controller trade-off: qwen-local entry control increased latency in candidates 3 and 8, and gpt-5.5 entry control in candidate-5 was costly and low quality.
rationale.rewrite_question: Question rewrite is rare, non-user-facing, and does not require tools or structured output. gpt-4.1-mini-cloud has been fast and negligible-cost for rewrites in candidates 2, 3, and 6, while qwen-local rewrite showed latency risk in candidate-1. Keeping rewrite on mini avoids compounding local-router latency and keeps the experiment focused on the retrieval sufficiency router.
